I farm only 5 mu, so I keep the whole wheat-maize rotation on all of it. I have been doing this a long time, and with only two people in the household, I will keep my plan practical and steady rather than risky. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water at the key stages instead of gambling on rain. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the fertilizer in up front, irrigate at the important growth periods, and manage weeds and disease with a small number of pesticide sprays. After wheat harvest, I will quickly prepare the land for maize, use hybrid seed for stronger yield, apply enough nitrogen for summer growth, irrigate when the crop is establishing and filling grain, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed. I will use rotary tillage because it matches my scale, saves labor, and works well in my wheat-maize system.
